faq.q: How much does The May Firm charge?
faq.a: The May Firm publishes a contingency fee, which means the fee is a share of what the case recovers and there is nothing to pay if it recovers nothing. The rate itself is not published, so ask for it in writing, along with how case expenses are handled and whether they come out of the recovery before or after the fee. The first consultation is free, which is the place to ask.

faq.q: Does The May Firm offer a free consultation?
faq.a: Yes. The May Firm publishes a free initial consultation. The intake line is published as open around the clock, the firm states it will visit clients in hospital or at home and it publishes material in Spanish.

faq.q: Where does The May Firm have offices?
faq.a: The May Firm publishes eight offices, among them Fresno, Long Beach, Bakersfield and Chula Vista. Addresses and the Google listing behind each one are on this profile under Offices.

faq.q: Who are the attorneys at The May Firm?
faq.a: The May Firm names 14 attorneys on its own site, and each is listed on this profile with the page we read them from. They have not been checked against a state register: California does not publish an attorney register we can query, so licensure is not verified here. The state's own attorney search is the place to check it.

faq.q: Are the case results The May Firm publishes verified?
faq.a: No. The May Firm publishes ten case results with amounts on its own site. We counted them and we did not confirm them: the figures are the firm's. Pillar B scores whether a firm publishes outcomes and discloses them properly, including whether a prior-results disclaimer appears beside them, not whether the amounts are right. Past results do not predict another case.

faq.q: What has Law Firm Listings verified about The May Firm?
faq.a: The May Firm scores 77 and sits at Certified. Passed: website and footprint. Could not be answered from any public source and therefore counts neither for nor against the firm: licensure, discipline and entity registration. Every row of the scorecard above names where the value came from and when it was read. Nothing on this profile was supplied by the firm for payment, and no placement here can be bought.

json_ld_descriptions: Robert May founded The May Firm on the core principles he learned growing up in a loving, hard-working, blue-collar family in Santa Maria. The lessons he learned from his parents are abundantly apparent in the day-to-day operation of his firm. They instilled in Robert and his four siblings the sincere desire to help people to the best of their ability. By example and by encouragement, Robert’s parents also taught Robert and his siblings the value of a solid work ethic.  Robert’s father, a concrete salesman, took exceptionally good care of his customers, treating each one like family and always going the extra mile to help them with whatever problem they had. Robert and his brothers follow in their father’s footsteps in the personal and exceptionally dedicated way they take care of their clients at The May Firm.  As you step inside the doorway of The May Firm, you will immediately notice there’s a difference. You won’t encounter a stuffy, overly pretentious office space. Instead, you’ll enter an environment where you’ll immediately feel right at home. You will notice Robert’s surfboard hanging on the wall and the photographs of him riding the big waves all over the world! You will be welcomed by the friendliest staff found in any law firm. They will treat you like family from the moment you meet them.  The most popular staff member with clients is Copper the dog, a super friendly vizsla named after one of the main characters in Disney’s The Fox & the Hound. His red canine nose immediately recognizes every client, and he is always happy to greet and comfort them. Even the delivery people love him! While Cooper loves everyone, his primary human is Cameron May, Robert and Garrett’s younger brother, who works as a senior case manager at the firm.
